# Le008 — `\S\X` (8-bit shift) directive: misuse, chaining, or apostrophe-after-`\S\`

## Description

`\S\x` adds 0x80 to the next single ASCII character `x` to address the upper half of the active ISO-8859 page. It is a one-character operator. Defects: parser closes the string when the byte after `\S\` is an apostrophe (`'\S\'`), treats the directive as multi-character (`\S\xy`), chains it (`\S\\S\E`), or recurses into nested directive parsing (`\S\\X\41`).

## Reproducer recipe

`'abc\S\'def'` (the byte after `\S\` is an apostrophe — the string is seven characters, not closed early); `'caf\S\\S\i'` (illegal chaining).

## Expected kernel behavior

spec mandates `\S\` consumes exactly the byte after the second `\` literally; do not recurse, do not close the string on that byte. Treat `\S\\` as `\S\` followed by `\` only outside another directive.

## Notes

Cross-oracle: pure-Python Part-21 validator rejects (reject(E_STRING_OPEN)); OCCT silently accepts (load is `empty`). OCC auto-heals a spec-level violation.
